subject: Hosted trial suitability — endpoint mapping, ratecaps, and VPC signals
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@finlytics.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + a couple clarifying asks after today's demo

Hi Martin / Priya —

Thanks again for jumping on the demo earlier — appreciate the thoughtful questions. I promised a short follow-up with the items we need to validate so we can recommend the right onboarding path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). To keep this tight, two buckets: traffic/security signals and ops constraints. Would you reply with the short answers below?

Traffic / API usage signals (helps us size endpoints and recommend ratecaps):
- Which endpoints did you most heavily test today? (generation, chat, embeddings, rerank)
- Peak QPS you expect in production (burst QPS vs steady-state)?
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + expected model response) for each endpoint
- Are there predictable daily/weekly seasonality windows (e.g., batch nightly jobs)?

Security / architecture signals (help choose Hosted vs Private/Dedicated):
- Is EU data residency required? If yes, is it strict (data must stay in EU) or flexible with contractual controls?
- Do you require VPC peering / private connectivity or is public HTTPS with IP allowlist sufficient?
- Regulatory/compliance checks we should know about (SOC2, DPA, custom questionnaire)

Ops / integration questions:
- Is SSO or SAML required for user access to a console?
- Any specific SLA targets (p95 latency targets, uptime)?

Next steps I propose after your answers:
1) If signals point to straightforward production traffic and no strict residency/VPC need -> propose a hosted trial in EU region with a sandbox slice and a per-endpoint ratecap matrix.
2) If you need strict residency or private networking -> we map to Dedicated or Private and include capacity lead times.

If it's helpful, I can also propose a 30-minute pilot planning call for Friday (Aug 11) to lock this down.

Thanks — I looped Ben (solutions) on this for technical scope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + a couple clarifying asks after today's demo

Hi Marissa —

Thanks, really helpful list. Answers below to the best of our current planning:

Traffic / API usage signals:
- Endpoints: primarily embeddings (for similarity search) and generation/chat for contextual prompts. Embeddings will be by far the highest QPS.
- Peak QPS (burst): embeddings up to ~350 QPS for short windows (1–3 minutes) during indexing runs. Steady-state QPS: ~40–60 QPS. Generation/chat peak ~30 QPS.
- Avg tokens: embeddings small (1–3 tokens for input IDs, we send short chunks). Generation/chat avg prompt+response ~400 tokens.
- Seasonality: nightly bulk indexing (02:00–03:30 CET) and periodic batch re-embeds on weekends.

Security / architecture:
- EU residency: yes, data and logs must remain in EU. We can accept contractual controls but prefer hosting physically in EU.
- Connectivity: public HTTPS + IP allowlist is fine for now, but we may require VPC peering if we move to private deployment later.
- Compliance: we will be requesting a standard security questionnaire. I attached our security profile so you can see the controls we're most focused on (Encryption at rest, access logging, retention windows).

Ops / integration:
- SSO: SAML would be nice for console access but it's not blocking for now.
- SLA: p95 token latency targets under 200ms for embeddings; generation can be higher (we understand variability), uptime expectations: standard enterprise SLA (99.9%).

We'd be open to a hosted EU trial if you can guarantee residency and provide a sandbox slice that can handle the nightly burst.

Thanks —
Martin
Martin Lopez
Head of Data Infrastructure, Finlytics
martin.lopez@finlytics.com

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and Martin's answers — signals are pretty clear: EU residency required, high embedding bursts overnight, and IP allowlist currently acceptable. Recommended next steps from our side (short):

1) Hosted EU trial (preferred):
   - Provision an EU-hosted sandbox slice pinned to an EU region for data residency.
   - Configure an embeddings endpoint with a burstable ratecap profile: steady 60 QPS, burstable to 400 QPS with token-based throttling and short warmup.
   - Set generation/chat endpoint with p95 latency monitoring; allow Slack-based alerts to Finlytics ops.

2) Docs + compliance:
   - Send SOC2 report + DPA + brief note on encryption-at-rest and KMS options. (I'll attach the SOC2 stub and DPA links in the HubSpot record.)

3) Pilot plan (mutual action items):
   - 2-week sandbox pilot -> validate embedding throughput and nightly batch window.
   - Pre-validate IP allowlist and SAML (if they want to test SSO).
   - On success, propose a follow-up to discuss Dedicated pool sizing for sustained throughput or Private VPC if they require direct peering.

I can draft the pilot proposal if you want; recommend we schedule 30m on Aug 11 (EMEA-friendly time) to align.

—Ben

Hi Martin / Priya —

Appreciate the quick answers — that gives us everything to put forward a pilot plan that matches your signals. Attached is a concise one-pager (redwood-hosted-pilot-proposal.pdf) outlining what we recommend for a 2-week sandbox pilot in the EU:

Highlights (TL;DR):
- Region & residency: EU-hosted sandbox with logs + KV cache retained in EU (meets your residency ask).
- Endpoints: embeddings endpoint (primary) + generation/chat endpoint.
- Ratecaps: embeddings steady 60 QPS, burst to 400 QPS for short windows during overnight indexing (we'll instrument token-based throttling and circuit-breakers).
- Observability: p95 latency and error dashboards, Slack alerts; we will share a transient API key for the sandbox with IP allowlist.
- Compliance: SOC2 report + DPA attached/linked in the Drive folder.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the pilot scope & acceptance criteria (embedding throughput, nightly indexing success).
2) We schedule a 30-minute kickoff (suggest Aug 11, 09:00–09:30 CET). Please tell us if that slot works or propose one.
3) We provision the sandbox and share IP allowlist steps + temporary credentials.

If the pilot validates the burst profile we can propose Dedicated sizing or Private options with lead times documented in the pilot wrap-up.
